format: Text with inline TeX in $...$. The correct choice is at index answer; the app shuffles the choices.

questions.question: When does a circuit need transmission-line analysis?
choices: When its length is a sizeable fraction of a wavelength (say more than $\lambda/100$)
Only when the frequency is above 1 GHz
Only when the wires are coaxial
questions.explain: Below that, the phase change along the wire is negligible and lumped circuit theory works.

questions.question: Characteristic impedance of a lossless line?
questions.explain: Lossless means $R'=G'=0$ in $Z_0=\sqrt{(R'+j\omega L')/(G'+j\omega C')}$.

questions.question: Phase velocity on a lossless line?
questions.explain: $\beta=\omega\sqrt{L'C'}$ and $u_p=\omega/\beta$.

questions.question: Input impedance of a $50\ \Omega$ line of any length ending in $50\ \Omega$?
questions.explain: A matched line has no reflection, so $Z_{in}=Z_0$ at every point.

questions.question: Input impedance of a quarter-wave line ending in $Z_L$?
questions.explain: $\tan\beta\ell\to\infty$ at $\ell=\lambda/4$, which leaves $Z_{in}=Z_0^2/Z_L$.

questions.question: Input impedance of a half-wave lossless line ending in $Z_L$?
questions.explain: $\tan\beta\ell=0$ at $\ell=\lambda/2$, so the line repeats its load.

questions.question: A short-circuited lossless stub shorter than $\lambda/4$ looks like
questions.explain: $Z_{in}=jZ_0\tan\beta\ell$ is positive imaginary for $0<\beta\ell<\pi/2$.

questions.question: Reflection coefficient for a $100\ \Omega$ load on a $50\ \Omega$ line?
VSWR when $|\Gamma|=1/3$?
$\Gamma$ for a short circuit?
How far apart are adjacent voltage maxima on a standing wave?
questions.explain: The pattern $|V(z)|$ repeats every half wavelength. A maximum and the next minimum are $\lambda/4$ apart.

questions.question: What fraction of incident power reaches a load with $|\Gamma|=0.5$?
On a line with a purely resistive load $R_L>Z_0$, where is the first voltage maximum?
questions.explain: $\Gamma$ is real and positive, so $\theta_r=0$ and $d_{\max}=0$.

questions.question: Where is a matched load on the Smith chart?
questions.explain: $z_L=1$ gives $\Gamma=0$, the centre of the chart.

questions.question: Moving from the load toward the generator rotates you on the Smith chart
questions.explain: $\Gamma(d)=\Gamma e^{-j2\beta d}$: the angle decreases, which is clockwise.

questions.question: How much line length is one full trip around the Smith chart?
questions.explain: $2\beta d=2\pi$ when $d=\lambda/2$.

questions.question: How do you turn an impedance into an admittance on the Smith chart?
choices: Go to the point diametrically opposite
Reflect it about the horizontal axis
questions.explain: Opposite points are a quarter wave apart, and a quarter-wave line inverts normalized impedance.

questions.question: The outer circle of the Smith chart holds loads that are
questions.explain: $|\Gamma|=1$ there: no power is absorbed.

questions.question: A quarter-wave transformer matches a $200\ \Omega$ load to a $50\ \Omega$ line. Its impedance?
questions.explain: $Z_{0,\lambda/4}=\sqrt{Z_0Z_L}=\sqrt{50\cdot200}$.

questions.question: A single shunt stub matches by
choices: Cancelling the susceptance at a point where $y=1+jb$
questions.explain: Move along the line until $\mathrm{Re}\{y\}=1$, then add a stub with susceptance $-b$.

questions.question: A quarter-wave transformer on its own can directly match
questions.explain: $\sqrt{Z_0Z_L}$ must be real. A complex load first needs a length of line to make it real.

questions.question: Why are shunt stubs often preferred to series stubs?
choices: They are easier to build: just tee a stub onto the line
They never need a short circuit
questions.explain: A series stub needs the main line to be cut, which is awkward in coax or microstrip.

questions.question: A step travels down a line. Its first value at the input is
questions.explain: Before any reflection returns, the line looks like a resistor $Z_0$.

questions.question: Final steady-state voltage on a lossless line after a step?
questions.explain: At DC the line is just a wire: a voltage divider of $R_s$ and $R_L$.

questions.question: What does a bounce diagram plot?
choices: Each wave's voltage against position and time, zig-zagging between the ends
questions.explain: Each leg adds a reflected wave, and summing them gives $V(z,t)$.

questions.question: With $R_s=R_L=Z_0$, how many reflections occur?
questions.explain: Both ends are matched, so $\Gamma_L=\Gamma_g=0$.
